record.detail: pick — 1. do the thing (recommended) · 2. skip

cases.why: CONSTRUCTED — regression bar for [[who-needs-me.py Omits a Pane That Has an Open Gate]]. The sibling defect was file-existence as the gate test: the hook deleted the record on ANY later event, so a background task completing erased an open gate. The fix made `state: answered` the only clearing signal. This case pins it: an answered record stays out of the feed even though its file is present.

record.detail: later (on the next live call): run /vault-cli:session-close

cases.why: CONSTRUCTED — the widening trap. A `later (on <trigger>):` deferral that merely mentions session-close must never become reapable: widening a prefix test into a containment test is exactly how a false-negative fix becomes a false positive. No live instance existed on 2026-09-19 (all three live `later (on …)` closers omitted session-close), but `later (on …)` is in routine fleet use, so the collision is a matter of time rather than of possibility.
